deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a draft, in Riemann's hand, of a Göttingen lecture announcement (Vorlesungsankündigung for the Index Scholarum / Vorlesungsverzeichnis), written first in Latin and then in German.

Latin: 'Bernhardus Riemann Dr. Theoriam gravitatis, electricitatis & magnetismi mathematicam docebit diebb. Lun. Mart. Jov. & Ven. h. VIII-IX; Functiones ellipticas tractabit iisdem diebb. h. XI-XII.' In English: Dr. Bernhard Riemann will teach the mathematical theory of gravitation, electricity and magnetism on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 8 to 9; he will treat elliptic functions on the same days from 11 to 12.

German: 'Dr. Riemann wird die mathematische Theorie der Schwere, Magnetismus und der Electricität vortragen. Mont. Dienst. Donn. u. Freit. v. 8-9 Uhr, und an denselben Wochentagen v. 11-12 Uhr über elliptische Functionen lesen.'

The corrections show how the text was drafted:
- Riemann first began with the elliptic-functions course ('Functiones ellipticas tractabit') and struck it out, so that the physics course is announced first.
- He struck a word after 'docebit' (probably 'quaternis', i.e. 'on four [days]') and replaced it with the explicit list of days.
- In the German version he struck 'der Electricität' after 'Schwere' and placed it after 'Magnetismus'. In the Latin he added '& electricitatis' interlinearly above 'magnetismi'. The ordering of electricity and magnetism was evidently being adjusted.

Context: the course 'Schwere, Elektricität und Magnetismus' is the one Hattendorff later edited (1876) from Riemann's lectures, which I believe date to the summer semester of 1861. The elliptic-functions course corresponds to the lectures later edited by H. Stahl (1899). Riemann gave such lectures in more than one semester. The date of this draft is uncertain: the reverse-side show-through mentions 1855, but it may be unrelated to this text.

deep.surprise_reason: Purely administrative draft of a lecture announcement; Riemann's lecturing on both topics is well documented. Its only interest is biographical: the drafting order and the day/hour schedule.

checkable.asserts: Trivial bookkeeping: two courses, each 4 days x 1 hour, give 8 weekly lecture hours (no mathematical content on the page).

transcription_corrections: The struck word after 'docebit' is likely 'quaternis' ('on four [days]'), replaced by the explicit list of days; the image supports this reading.
Above the struck 'Functiones ellipticas tractabit' in line 1 there is a small interlinear word (apparently a repeated 'tractabit') that is also cancelled.

The interlinear '& electricitatis' stands above 'magnetismi mathematicam'. It appears to reflect a reordering parallel to the German, where 'der Electricität' is struck after 'Schwere' and re-inserted after 'Magnetismus'. The 'electricitatis' at the end of line 1 may itself be overwritten or cancelled; this is unclear in the image.
Expanded forms: 'diebb.' = diebus; 'Lun. Mart. Jov. & Ven.' = Lunae, Martis, Jovis et Veneris (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri); 'h' = horis.
